name: Why a well's oil rate declines

myth.myth: A well keeps producing at a constant rate until the oil runs out
myth.correction: The rate falls as reservoir pressure depletes and the water share of the produced liquid grows

statements.statement: The production rate depends on the pressure difference between the reservoir and the well, the drawdown.
As fluids are withdrawn, reservoir pressure declines unless it is maintained, so the achievable rate drops.
After water breakthrough the water cut rises, so the oil share of the produced liquid falls.
Decline-curve analysis fits the falling rate to forecast future production.

data_meaning.text: In daily production data the oil rate of a well drifts down over months, with steps when the choke or the well status changes.

analogy: Like forecasting a degrading time series: fit a trend to noisy history, but first flag the step changes - choke changes and shut-ins are regime switches, not trend.
